lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
lesson.summary: Fractions bigger than one: mixed numbers, improper fractions, converting both ways and adding within a whole.
lesson.unit: Topic 8: Mixed numbers and improper fractions
learning_objectives: Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers
Add and subtract fractions with the same bottom number

standards.text: Count up and down in hundredths; recognise and write fractions greater than 1; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator

success_criteria: I can write a mixed number from a picture
I can change an improper fraction to a mixed number and back
I can add fractions with the same bottom number
lesson.real_life: Sharing naan and pizza, measuring rice and milk in a recipe, and counting slices at a party.

blocks.alt: Slices of pepperoni pizza on an orange background
blocks.caption: A pizza cut into slices shows fractions bigger than one whole.
blocks.credit: Photo by Tamas Pap on Unsplash
blocks.say: It is Eid lunch. Ayesha's family has pizza and naan. Some pieces are bigger than one whole. We can write them in two ways. Let's find out how.

blocks.markdown:
A **mixed number** has a whole part and a fraction part: 1 3/4.

7 quarters = 1 whole and 3 quarters = 1 3/4.
blocks.say: Cut a naan into quarters. Four quarters make one whole naan. Now take seven quarters. That is one whole naan and three quarters left over. We write it as a mixed number: one and three quarters, or 1 3/4.

scenes.caption: 4 quarters = 1 whole
scenes.say: Here is one whole naan, cut into four quarters. All four are shaded.

scenes.caption: 7 quarters
scenes.say: Add three more quarters. That is seven quarters in all.
One whole and three quarters. We write it 1 3/4.

blocks.alt: Two pizza diagrams: one whole pizza and three quarters, labelled 1 3/4
blocks.say: Seven quarters make one whole pizza and three quarters. We write one and three quarters.

question.prompt: How many quarters make one whole?

blocks.text: Stop 2: Write it and read it

blocks.markdown:
Say **the whole, then and, then the fraction**: 2 1/2 is two and a half.

3 1/3 is three and one third.
blocks.say: Read a mixed number in words. Two and one half is 2 1/2. Say the whole first, then 'and', then the fraction. Mind the small words: one and one half, not one one-half.

blocks.alt: Two whole naans and one half naan make 2 1/2.
blocks.caption: Two whole naans and one half naan make 2 1/2.

question.explanation: 2 1/2 is two wholes and a half.

blocks.title: The naan that is more than one
blocks.transcript: This is Uncle Hamid. He bakes naan for the Eid lunch in Karachi. He cuts one naan into four equal quarters. Each piece is one quarter. Now he has seven quarters. That is more than one whole naan. One whole naan and three quarters. We write it as one and three quarters. Seven quarters is one and three quarters. Shukriya, Uncle Hamid!
blocks.caption: A baker cuts naan into quarters and turns seven quarters into a mixed number.

points: A mixed number has a whole part and a fraction part

blocks.say: Remember. Four quarters make a whole. A mixed number is a whole and a fraction.

blocks.markdown:
To change **improper to mixed**: group by the bottom number. Count the wholes, then the leftover.

13/4: 13 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 1, so 3 1/4.
blocks.say: Here is a big fraction: 13 quarters. Group them in fours. Each group of four is one whole. How many full groups are there? Three groups make 12 quarters. One quarter is left over. So 13/4 = 3 1/4.

scenes.caption: 3 wholes
scenes.say: Make groups of four. Each group is one whole. Three full groups.
One quarter is left over. So 13/4 is 3 wholes and 1 quarter.

question.prompt: How many whole ones are in 17/4?
question.explanation: Four groups of four make 16, and 1 quarter is left. So 17/4 = 4 1/4.

blocks.markdown:
To change **mixed to improper**: multiply the whole by the bottom, then add the top.

2 3/4 = (2 × 4 + 3)/4 = 11/4.
blocks.say: Now go back. Two and three quarters is 2 3/4. Each whole has four quarters. Two wholes are eight quarters. Add the three more quarters. Eight add three makes eleven. So 2 3/4 = 11/4.

blocks.title: Quarter strips
materials: Paper strips cut into 4 equal parts
instructions: Colour 13 quarters across three strips of four, and one spare.
Count the full strips. That is the whole part.
Count the spare quarters. That is the fraction part.

points: Improper to mixed: group by the bottom
Mixed to improper: whole × bottom + top
The bottom number stays the same
blocks.say: Remember. Improper to mixed: group and count. Mixed to improper: whole times bottom, then add the top.

blocks.markdown:
On a number line, **1 1/4** sits one quarter past 1.

Count the quarters: 1, 1 1/4, 1 1/2, 1 3/4, 2.
blocks.say: Let's put mixed numbers on a number line. The line goes from 0 to 2. Halfway is one. Quarters sit between each whole. One and one quarter sits just after 1.

scenes.say: Start at 1. Each step is one quarter.
One step: 1 1/4. Two steps: 1 1/2. Three steps: 1 3/4.
One more step reaches 2 wholes, which is 8 quarters.

question.prompt: Which mixed number is closer to 2?
question.explanation: 1 4/5 is only one fifth away from 2. 1 1/5 is four fifths away.

blocks.markdown:
**Compare the wholes first**, then the fractions.

1 3/5 < 1 4/5.
blocks.say: Compare mixed numbers. Look at the whole first. Then the fraction. One and three fifths is smaller than one and four fifths. Three fifths is less than four fifths.

question.explanation: Four fifths is more than two fifths, so 1 4/5 is bigger.

question.prompt: A pizza is cut into 8 slices. Ali eats 3 slices and Sam eats 4. How many eighths are eaten?
question.hint: Add the tops. Keep the bottom.

blocks.markdown:
**Same bottom number**: add the tops and keep the bottom. 3/8 + 4/8 = 7/8.

Do not add the bottoms.
blocks.say: Add 3/8 and 4/8. The bottoms are the same, so just add the tops. Three eighths and four eighths make seven eighths. The bottom number stays eight.

scenes.say: Add four more eighths. Seven eighths in all.
Seven eighths. The pizza is still cut into eight.
